subject: Kitchenware.ai perf qualification: eval harness onboarding & repro runbook
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <sgupta@kitchenware.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@kitchenware.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@kitchenware.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + SLO targets (post-demo)

Rishi / team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — clear product and nice walkthrough of the streaming behavior. Per our internal follow-up we want to lock down a few concrete targets and next steps for the perf qualification so we can take this to procurement. High‑level asks from our side: 

- Latency targets: p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 250ms for 256-token prompts (interactive UI).
- Throughput/concurrency: steady 200 qps with 500 concurrent users; bursty traffic pattern up to 1k qps sustained for ~30s during promotions.
- Streaming requirements: first-token within 120ms, subsequent token streaming with <30ms gap on average; support for partial output (we will use SSE/HTTP streaming).
- Reproducibility: We need a reproducible harness to run in our lab (we can run your image or you provide a compatible client).

Can you confirm Redwood can reproduce those numbers against a realistic prompt set, and share what you need from us (sanitized prompts, traffic shape, any credentials)? Also cc'd Elena from ops — please loop procurement on what artifacts they will need for the commitment.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood shares a short repro-runbook + initial prompt pack (sanitized).
2) We schedule a 60-min handoff with your SE to run the harness the week of Aug 30.
3) If results look good, procurement will ask for pricing and SLA language.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Platform
Kitchenware.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <sgupta@kitchenware.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@kitchenware.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@kitchenware.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + SLO targets (post-demo)

Samir — great to meet you and thanks for the clear targets. Confirm Redwood can run an initial qualification that aligns with the bullets you listed. Attached are the artifacts we discussed: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sanitized starter pack) and eval-harness-spec.pdf (measurement definitions + infra options). I also exported a short repro-runbook.md that outlines exact steps to reproduce runs locally or in your cloud.

High-level notes / clarifications:
- Latency: our measurements are for end‑to‑end token latency; p95 depends significantly on sequence length distribution and whether the KV cache is warm. Our recommendation: we run both cold and warm runs — warm means prepopulating KV cache with 256-token prefixes.
- Throughput: we will use a closed-loop generator to emulate concurrent sessions (200 steady qps) and an open-loop Poisson burst profile for the 1k qps short bursts. We will share the exact driver config (RPS, ramp, concurrency).
- Streaming: Redwood supports SSE and chunked HTTP streaming. For first-token latency we measure from request time to first byte delivered. For streaming inter-token gaps we instrument per-token arrival timestamps.

Ask from you:
1) Confirm which model variant you want us to evaluate (e.g., rl-13b-v2 or open-13b-quant). If uncertain, we can propose two: a high‑accuracy variant and a quantized cost‑optimized one.
2) Sign off on the attached prompt_set_v1.jsonl (it is sanitized but please confirm no PII).
3) Confirm a 60‑min slot the week of Aug 30 for an SE‑led handoff; options I have are Mon Aug 30 10:00–12:00 PDT or Tue Aug 31 14:00–16:00 PDT.

I'll drop the eval harness spec into the Jira ticket INF-2345 and loop in Marissa (measurement lead) and Neha (SRE) to propose the concrete run schedule.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
+1 (555) 213-0098

Attachment stubs: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (text), eval-harness-spec.pdf (pdf), repro-runbook.md (text)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <sgupta@kitchenware.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@kitchenware.ai>, Procurement <procurement@kitchenware.ai>
Date: 2027-08-23T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + SLO targets (post-demo) — measurement defs + reproducibility checklist

Adding a few concrete measurement definitions so we have the same topline semantics during the run: 

- Measurement window: 10-minute warmup followed by 30-minute steady window (for steady 200 qps). Bursts: three 30s open-loop spikes to 1k qps separated by 5m.
- Latency calculus: p50/p95/p99 measured on per‑request first-byte time (end‑to‑end). For streaming, we report first_token_latency (ms) and median inter_token_gap (ms) across all streams.
- Sequence length buckets: 64/128/256/512 tokens — we will report SLOs per bucket.
- Repeatability: each experiment is run 3 independent times (different seeds) and we report mean + stddev. We instrument CPU/GPU utilization, kernel times, and queue lengths.
- Determinism knobs: sampling seed, temperature, top_p set in harness; for quality parity tests we will run greedy/beam settings.

Repro checklist for your team to enable a full independent run: 
- Confirm model variant name and any quantization/profile used.
- Provide sanitized prompt file (attached is our starter — confirm).
- If possible, provide a small subset of traffic traces (anonymized) to match session patterns.
- Allow Redwood SE to run a short remote test (we can run on Windows/Ubuntu containers) or provide access to a test cluster with 4xA100 v4-equivalents.

I've put a short runbook into INF-2345 with exact driver commands and environment variables (repro-runbook.md attachment). Neha — can you validate the GPU warmup procedure and typical prefetch settings we recommend?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Measurement Lead, Redwood Inference

Rishi / Marissa / Neha — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple quick replies: 

- Model variant: please run the high‑accuracy and the quantized candidate (we're evaluating cost/latency tradeoffs).
- Prompt pack: Elena confirms the starter pack is clean. We will add one more edge-case prompt and send by EOD Aug 25.
- Hand‑off time: Tue Aug 31 14:00 PDT works for us — please send a calendar invite.
- Procurement: I'll start the internal PR and will need the eval artifacts + raw harness logs for SLA review. Please include an exportable CSV of the run metrics.

If you can also include a short note on how Redwood computes billing for streaming responses (token counting rules) that will speed legal signoff.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the handoff.

Samir
